title: Slicing Strings
description: Grab a single letter or a whole section out of a string.

content.text: A string is a row of characters in order, like carriages in a train. It is numbered exactly like a list: the first one is number 0.

content.title: Each letter has an index
content.caption: Index 0 is the first letter. Negative numbers count back from the end, so index -1 is always the last letter.

content.value: Six letters means the valid indexes are 0 to 5. Asking for `word[6]` raises an `IndexError`, the same error a list gives when you go past the end.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: Index -1 is always the last letter. The last letter of `cake` is `e`.

items: A **slice** takes several letters at once.
Write a start index, a colon, and a stop index.
The slice runs **up to** the stop index but does **not include** it.
Number of letters you get = stop minus start.
content.title: The slice rule

parts.label: colon
parts.note: Means: a range, not one letter.

parts.label: stop
parts.note: The first index left out. You get 0 and 1, then it stops just short of 2.

content.caption: `word[2:5]` gives indexes 2, 3 and 4: three letters, because 5 - 2 is 3.

content.value: Move the two handles below and watch which tiles light up. The stop number is the first letter left out.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: Start at index 1 (`a`) and stop just before index 4: indexes 1, 2 and 3 give `ana`.

items.sub: No start: begins at the beginning.
No stop: runs to the end.

content.title: Python fills in the obvious answer

content.value:
word = "Python"

print(word[:2])    # from the start
print(word[2:])    # to the end
print(word[-3:])   # the last three letters
print(word)        # unchanged
content.caption: A slice is a new string: `word` itself never changes

items.title: Index past the end
items.text: One letter that is not there: `IndexError`.

items.title: Slice past the end
items.text: Python quietly stops at the end: `thon`. If start and stop cross over, you get an empty string, not a crash.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `[-3:]` starts three letters from the end and runs to the end.

editorCode:
secret = "AbraCadabra"

print(secret[0:4])    # Abra
print(secret[4:])     # Cadabra
print(secret[-1])     # a
print("Unchanged:", secret)

quiz.question: If word = 'Magic', what does word[0] print?
quiz.explain: Counting starts at 0, so index 0 is the very first letter.

quiz.question: For word = 'Python', what does word[1:4] give?
quiz.explain: It takes indexes 1, 2 and 3 and stops before 4, giving three letters: y, t and h.

quiz.question: Which slice gives the LAST two letters of any string?
quiz.explain: A negative start counts back from the end, so [-2:] means from two before the end onwards. word[-2] would give just one letter.
